newsitem.title: UK: BT to axe 5,000 jobs, union says.
newsitem.headline: BT to axe 5,000 jobs, union says.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Thursday said it had discussed possible redundancies with union officials, but declined to confirm the union's claim that up to 5,000 jobs would go.
The Communication Workers' Union issued a statement saying that the clerical and engineering jobs would be lost from BT's Network and System Operations division, which employs 40,000 people.
The union described the possible job losses as "totally unacceptable" and accused BT of understaffing.
A spokesman for BT said the issue had been raised at a regular meeting with the union this week, but said "I don't know where they got that figure (5,000) from."
"We are very disappointed that they have chosen to discuss publicly things that were discussed in private," he added.
He said that job losses were an inevitable consequence of new technology.
"We would only have job losses when we can continue to provide the service that we do. Its too early to start talking about numbers."

Earlier on Thursday, BT announced pretax profits for the first quarter of the current financial year of 881 million pounds ($1.4 billion), up 1.4 percent from a year earlier. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
